namespace Mathoverflow486451

/-- There exists a semiring with a unique left maximal ideal but more than one right maximal ideals. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 16]
theorem exists_semiring_unique_left_maximal_not_unique_right_maximal :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : Semiring R), (∃! I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal) ∧
      ∃ I J : Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ, I.IsMaximal ∧ J.IsMaximal ∧ I ≠ J := by
  sorry

/-- There exists a semiring with a unique left maximal ideal and a unique right maximal ideal
which are not the same as sets.

This has been shown by Goran Žužić and Moritz Firsching using an experimental pipeline:
An example is the monoid algebra of the monoid of maps from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$
over $\mathbb{N}$.
 -/
@[category research solved, AMS 16, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/f7502b9ed3e32d193ab8fee53d2e28f7d67f2dc3/FormalConjectures/Mathoverflow/486451.lean#L333"]
theorem exists_semiring_unique_left_right_maximal_ne :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ (R : Type) (_ : Semiring R) (hI : ∃! I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal)
      (hJ : ∃! J : Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ, J.IsMaximal),
        (hI.choose : Set R) ≠ MulOpposite.op ⁻¹' hJ.choose := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow486451

reformulations.difference: The source asks for multiple maximal right ideals of R; Lean represents them as maximal left ideals of the opposite semiring Rᵐᵒᵖ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Pullback along MulOpposite.op gives an order isomorphism from Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ to RightIdeal R: opposite left multiplication becomes original right multiplication. This preserves properness, maximality, and distinctness. The full equivalence with the formulation using RightIdeal R was proved as Review486451.first_full_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Rather than explicitly naming the two unique maximal ideals on R, Lean existentially quantifies their unique-existence proofs, chooses their witnesses, and pulls the opposite ideal back to a subset of R.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Each choice satisfies maximality and uniqueness by choose_spec, and uniqueness forces it to equal any explicitly named maximal ideal. Under the opposite-ideal/right-ideal order isomorphism, the right ideal’s carrier is exactly MulOpposite.op ⁻¹' hJ.choose. Thus the inequality compares the intended subsets of R. Together with True ↔ P being equivalent to P, this yields precisely the source’s positive existence claim. The full equivalence was proved as Review486451.second_full_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes:
Both declarations faithfully express the source’s existence questions. Boundary checks established that maximality implies Nontrivial R, trivial semirings have no maximal ideals, and the uniqueness assumptions are satisfiable. Finite carrier enumeration for ZMod 1, 2, 3, and 6 gave the expected maximal-ideal counts on both sides. The equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency.

The MathOverflow answer confirms the second theorem’s positive answer, example, and reported formal proof. The historical proof link was not accessed because it points to the prohibited repository. The accessible source does not supply a resolution of the first question, so its research solved tag could not be independently substantiated; absence of a posted solution is not sufficient evidence to report a status error.
